To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the dynamics of multi-splike patterns for the one-dimentional Gray-Scott model can be characterized by a novel ODE-PDE Stefan problem.

(1) in the quasi-steady regime, a multi-spike solution can undergo a subcritical Hopf bifurcations in which the spike amplitues oscillate on an O( 1) time scale; (2) in the nonquasisteady regime, the spikes drift away from their equilibrium position due to the instability arising from the Hopf bifurcatin, and the resulting time-dependent solution is a travelling wave.

(a) the dynamics of a single spike is governed by the classical Fisher equation, (b) a collection of spikes undergoes oscillatory instabilities leading to oscillatory dynamics in the spike amptidues or locations, (c) the oscillations in the amplitudes are due to Hopf bifurcations in a quasi-steady Stefan problem, and (d) the drift instability of the spike layers is a Hopf bifuration in the full Stefan problem.
